newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse rises in illiquid market.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse rises in illiquid market.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange ended its two-hour session on Wednesday up 0.57 percent, pushed higher by a shortage of shares, stockbrokers said.
The all-share index closed at 500.26 points from 497.44 points on Tuesday.
Consumer credit firms made significant gains with Diac equipement rose 57 dirhams, Diac Maroc 19 dirhams and Sofac credit 14 dirhams to respectively 355, 559 and 515 dirhams.
"This was only due to illiquidity of these stocks," the broker said.
In the banking sector, blue chip, Wafabank, dropped 10 dirhams to close at 660 dirhams.
Newly-floated credit firm credor dipped 40 dirhams to 650 dirhams.
Mortgage bank, fell eight dirhams to close at 262 dirhams.
Banque Nationale pour le Developpement Economique, dipped six dirhams to close at 179 dirhams. Morocco said it would soon sell its 34.57 percent stake in the bank.
"Wafabank, Credor, Banque Marocaine pour le developpenent Economique and Credit Hotelier et Immobilier fell on profit taking," A broker at Casablanca-based Wafabourse said.

Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, one of the leading banks, gained 13 dirhams for the second day to close at 459 dirhams. BMCE plans to cut its interest rate by 0.25 percent on loans to small and medium enterprises starting from February 1.

ONA group, Morocco's largest private conglomerate, remained unchanged at 625 dirhams. The conglomerate, which holds stakes in more than 100 firms, is the first market capitalisation with more than 10 billion dirhams.
Second largest holding, Societe nationale d'Investissement, took seven dirhams to 575 dirhams.
The session best performer was ledible oil concern Lesieur which jumped 123 dirhams to 1565 dirhams.
Traded volume on the official market was 46.6 million dirhams from 58.1 million dirhams on Tuesday.
